name: BTC-social risk-on overlay — a SLOW base book whose exposure is TILTED by a low-turnover BTC-social regime
rationale: The high-turnover daily btc-social trigger already FAILED the Gate at deflated Sharpe 0.596. The honest re-run asks a different question: does BTC's SLOW social-attention regime carry information when used as a LOW-TURNOVER EXPOSURE TILT on a slow book, rather than as a daily entry trigger? This spec is the BASE BOOK: a weekly-rebalanced cross-sectional momentum long (ret over mom_lb above a fitted floor, held ~7d, no daily re-trigger). The overlay is NOT in this spec — it is applied by research/rerun_cohort.py as a per-bar market-wide size_multiplier = base*(lo + (hi-lo)*btc_social_regime), where btc_social_regime (research/social_norm.slow_social_regime) is a SLOW EWMA(W=20-40d) of BTC social_volume_accel, within-sample z-normalized, with hysteresis (ON z>+0.5 / OFF z<-0.5) and a min-dwell, so it flips only a handful of times per year. The size tilt adds/removes NO trades — it only scales exposure when the slow regime is risk-on vs risk-off. Pre-registered disconfirmers (rerun_cohort): the social tilt must beat (a) the flat-exposure baseline and (b) the SAME book tilted by an equal-turnover BTC-PRICE regime, and a within-regime time-shuffle placebo must NOT reproduce it. Falsified if any disconfirmer matches. The W/dwell free params are counted as trials in build_grid. Spot, long-only.
catalyst: slow positive cross-sectional momentum, exposure scaled by the slow BTC-social risk-on regime
